reason: I want to build the case, and folding the metal stock at the jig seems like a natural way to make its shell.
expectation: I expect a folded case or frame that can take insulation and refrigeration, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The cold packs will likely help keep the sample frozen, but I want to make the container first.

effect: The folding jig produced a case shell, so I can now add insulation.
reaction: The result was predictable and satisfying: the metal became the container I needed.
reason: Insulating the shell seems like the next practical step toward keeping the core cold.
expectation: I expect the felt to line or insulate the case, though it may still need refrigeration and cold packs.

alternatives.reason: Freezing the cold packs also seems necessary, but I want to finish the case structure first.

effect: The felt turned the shell into an insulated field case, ready for its cooling equipment.
reaction: That was a straightforward, sensible step.
reason: The refrigeration insert seems like the natural next part of the cold case.
expectation: I expect an actively cooled case, though it may still need the cold packs.

alternatives.reason: The packs may also be needed, but I want to install the refrigeration first.

effect: The refrigeration insert completed a case with a cradle for the lined core and a radiator that releases heat to the air.
reaction: The explanation of where the heat goes makes the cooling setup clearer.
reason: Freezing the cold packs is the only available combination and seems useful for keeping the core cold.
expectation: I expect the freezer to prepare the packs for use in the refrigerated case.

effect: The freezer conditioned the cold packs for temporary heat absorption during transfer; active refrigeration is needed to restore their capacity.
reaction: The distinction between temporary cold packs and active refrigeration is useful.
reason: Adding the conditioned packs to the refrigerated case is the only available combination and should prepare it to protect the core during transfer.
expectation: I expect the packs to fit into the case and provide temporary cooling support, though I do not know whether that completes the case.

effect: The case is complete: active refrigeration maintains about minus 45 degrees, while the packs provide a short buffer during power changes.
reaction: The power-change explanation made the packs' role clear and gave the finished case a satisfying purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Installing the refrigeration insert was most worthwhile because the explanation showed how the case moves heat out through its radiator.

leastWorthwhile.text: Folding and insulating the shell were sensible but predictable steps with little discovery.

surprise.text: The cold packs provide only a limited transfer buffer and need active refrigeration to restore their capacity.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each part had a clear role in building or cooling the case, although the final two combinations were the only ones offered.

continue.text: Yes. I am curious whether an intact core preserves a whole ridged fragment and what it might reveal.
